description: Distributed tracing with Zipkin, Jaeger, OpenTelemetry, and tracing patterns for Java microservices

questions.question: What is distributed tracing and why is it necessary for microservices?
questions.answer: Distributed tracing tracks requests as they flow through multiple services, creating complete request journey visualization. Necessary because: 1) Identify bottlenecks across services, 2) Debug failures in distributed systems, 3) Understand service dependencies, 4) Measure end-to-end latency. Example: User places order → API Gateway → Order Service → Payment Service → Inventory Service → Notification Service. Single trace shows: total latency 850ms, breakdown by service (Order 100ms, Payment 600ms, Inventory 50ms, Notification 100ms). Payment is bottleneck. Traditional logs scattered across services, correlation difficult. Trace shows causal relationships, parent-child spans, timing. Components: Trace (unique ID for request), Span (single operation), Tags (metadata), Logs (events within span). Tools: Zipkin, Jaeger, AWS X-Ray.
